description: Trigger discrimination for telemetry-contract design: what to emit and how requests correlate, versus hands-on instrumentation (observability-operator, manual-only), SLOs and alerting (slo-reliability-architect), redaction-rule authorship (sensitive-disclosure-guard), synthetic monitoring (synthetic-monitoring-architect), and platform infrastructure (cloud-architecture-decider).

cases.prompt: Design what our new checkout service should log, metric, and trace, and the correlation-ID scheme across the queue.
cases.reason: The emission contract and correlation scheme for a system under construction is this skill's design; no instrumentation run or SLO target is in view.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke observability-operator. Add the structured log statements and metric emitters to the running checkout service.
cases.reason: Hands-on instrumentation of a live system is observability-operator's (manual-only); this skill designs the contract and instruments nothing.

cases.prompt: Set the SLO targets, error budgets, and alerting thresholds for the checkout service.
cases.reason: SLO targets and alerting policy are slo-reliability-architect's scope; the telemetry contract feeds it, it does not own it.

cases.prompt: Define which fields must be masked in logs and the exact redaction rules.
cases.reason: Authoring redaction rules is sensitive-disclosure-guard's scope; the design composes those rules by reference.

cases.prompt: Design the scheduled production probes that exercise the checkout journey from outside.
cases.reason: Synthetic probes against the live app are synthetic-monitoring-architect's scope; this skill designs internal emission, not external checks.

cases.prompt: Choose the cloud platform and the infrastructure layout for our observability stack.
cases.reason: Platform and infrastructure decisions are cloud-architecture-decider's scope; the telemetry contract is platform-neutral.
